story.title: Fifth Oman Science Festival Opens with 570 Interactive STEM Activities

detail.extracted_title: Fifth Oman Science Festival Opens with 570 Interactive STEM Activities
detail.excerpt: Guided by the theme "Our Knowledge: The Compass of Our Future," thousands of students explore 22 scientific zones in Muscat as 87 Omani robotics competitors depart for Riyadh
detail.article_html:
Across the exhibition halls of the Oman Convention and Exhibition Centre in Muscat, theoretical classroom formulas have given way to particle physics simulations, autonomous drone corridors, and climate modeling laboratories. Patronized by Sultan bin Salim Al Habsi, Minister of Finance, and attended by Dr. Madiha bint Ahmed Al Shaibaniyah, Minister of Education, the fifth edition of the Oman Science Festival 2026 officially opened under the theme "Our Knowledge: The Compass of Our Future."

Running alongside the national send-off of 87 Omani students and mentors to the 17th Arab Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Championship in Riyadh, the festival brings together 570 interactive scientific activities across 22 specialized corners. Drawing public and private universities, research centers, military and security agencies, and international scientific delegations from Russia and Hungary, the week-long gathering turns Muscat into an open laboratory for young innovators.

Inside the 22 Specialized Scientific Corners

Rather than presenting static display boards, the fifth edition organizes its 570 workshops and live experiments around applied problem-solving. At the Ahmad Bin Majid Theatre and the Ibn Sina Theatre, students participate in live physics demonstrations, mathematics olympiads, and cybersecurity defense challenges. Saeed bin Juma Al Busaidi, Head of the Scientific Activities and Volunteering Section at the Ministry of Education and Supervisor of the Ahmad Bin Majid Theatre, noted that the theatrical programming pairs competitive coding and mental arithmetic with interactive stage experiments designed to make complex scientific principles accessible to families and school groups.

International science diplomacy also takes center stage. Russian scientific institutions are presenting two dedicated programs—"Wonders of the Universe" and "Bridges of Science"—introducing Omani students to peaceful nuclear energy applications, genetic wave research, particle physics, and deep-space astro-imaging, alongside interactive engineering exhibits hosted by visiting specialists from Hungary.

Military Simulation, Digital Command, and Climate Science

Several of the festival's busiest zones bridge youth education with sovereign operational technology. In the Military and Security Technologies Corner, supervised by Yousuf bin Abdullah Al Jabri, students test aerial drone navigation systems, air traffic control radar simulators, marine bridge navigation units, and virtual-reality firefighting environments. Visitors also examine two domestically deployed operational systems: the "Barq" digital leadership platform and the AEGIS safety and hazard-monitoring platform.

Nearby, the Environment Authority's Climate Change Corner guides students through physical and digital models of atmospheric warming. Amani bint Abdullah Al Aufi, Innovation Specialist at the Environment Authority, explained that the interactive experiments allow students to measure how industrial carbon dioxide emissions accelerate polar glacier melt and sea-level shifts, connecting global environmental metrics directly to Oman's national net-zero transition.

87 Omani Competitors Head to the Arab Robotics Championship

The opening of the Oman Science Festival coincided with a formal ceremony led by Majid bin Said Al Bahri, Undersecretary of the Ministry of Education for Administrative and Financial Affairs, honoring the Omani National Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Team ahead of their departure for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, from 5 to 9 November 2026.

Comprising 87 male and female students, technical supervisors, and accredited judges across 14 national teams, the delegation will represent the Sultanate at the 17th Arab Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Championship across eight rigorous categories, including RoboCup Junior, Sumo Robotics, Line Follower, Drone Maze, and Future Innovators—translating the curiosity nurtured in Oman's science halls directly onto the regional competitive stage.

detail.instagram_caption:
The fifth edition of the Oman Science Festival 2026 has opened at the Oman Convention and Exhibition Centre in Muscat under the theme "Our Knowledge: The Compass of Our Future." Patronized by Sultan bin Salim Al Habsi, Minister of Finance, in the presence of Dr. Madiha bint Ahmed Al Shaibaniyah, Minister of Education, the festival transforms Muscat into an interactive scientific laboratory for thousands of students and families.

Across the exhibition halls and national innovation stages, Omani youth are engaging directly with advanced science and engineering:

- 570 Interactive STEM Activities: Distributed across 22 specialized scientific corners, plus live mathematics, cybersecurity, and physics competitions at the Ahmad Bin Majid Theatre and Ibn Sina Theatre.
- Global & Sovereign Tech Zones: International delegations from Russia ("Wonders of the Universe" and "Bridges of Science") and Hungary join Omani military, aviation, and environmental agencies demonstrating drone navigation, the "Barq" digital leadership platform, VR firefighting, and climate modeling.
- 87 Omani Robotics Competitors Bound for Riyadh: Alongside the festival opening, the Ministry of Education honored 87 Omani students, supervisors, and judges across 14 national teams departing for the 17th Arab Robotics and AI Championship in Riyadh (5-9 November 2026).

Read the full story on Oman's next generation of scientists and engineers at omanspire.om (link in bio).

seo_metadata.featured_image_alt_text: Minimalist Swiss serigraph editorial illustration of a monumental brass-ochre astrolabe compass projecting light toward planetary rings and a robotic arm above Omani students.
seo_metadata.visual_prompt: Minimalist mid-century Swiss serigraph and lineless faceted geometric editorial illustration celebrating the Fifth Oman Science Festival and Omani youth scientific discovery and robotics. Monumental, surreal conceptual composition where a grand geometric brass-ochre navigational astrolabe and compass rose merges with sweeping modern Omani architectural arches, projecting dramatic diagonal chiaroscuro beams of cream off-white and marine teal light alongside clean geometric planetary rings and an abstract faceted robotics arm across a deep midnight navy sky. In small environmental scale, minimalist faceless geometric silhouettes of a young Omani male student in a crisp off-white dishdasha and kumma cap and a young Omani female student in a modest flowing black abaya and shayla headscarf standing at the base of the monumental compass plaza looking upward. Strictly lineless flat color planes with zero black comic outlines, zero facial features, zero floating arrows or glowing tablets, and subtle screenprint risograph paper grain texture. Curated high-contrast palette of deep midnight navy shadows, warm desert sand ochre, burnt terracotta coral, clean cream off-white, and a focused accent of marine teal. High-end New Yorker, Economist, and Monocle magazine cover art aesthetic. Strictly no realism, no text, no words, no letters, no typography, no labels, no signs, no numbers baked into the artwork, strictly no frame, no border, no white margin, no matting, seamless full bleed composition extending to all four edges.
